title: heap overflow in set_dealloc (setobject.c)
consumer: not established; the trigger is the upstream fix's own regression test
live_proof: measured, not asserted: the trigger runs on the pinned 3.13.7 ASan build (PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0) and reports ASAN:heap-buffer-overflow in a 216-byte region. Running it is the liveness proof -- a sanitizer report here means the defect is present in this tree.
fidelity: the trigger is upstream's own reproducer from the issue, run through the real interpreter rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it.
layer_note: measured: ASan reported a 216-byte region, at or under the 512 B SMALL_REQUEST_THRESHOLD

virtual-malloc.oracle: virtual profile, pymalloc stock on musl mallocng (tools/arms.json virtual-cpython): a fault in one of the case's fault_sites, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it
virtual-malloc.verdict_note: cause=24 pc=0x3f9615a8a0 in set_dealloc; by function: set_dealloc is where host ASan reported the access

virtual-nested-pools.oracle: virtual profile, pymalloc's blocks as child lifetimes (patch 0014, CDERIVE/CREVOKE; tools/arms.json virtual-cpython-pools): as virtual-malloc
virtual-nested-pools.verdict_note: cause=28 pc=0x3fa515aae4 in set_dealloc; by function: set_dealloc is where host ASan reported the access

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: completion while the block's arena stays live: pymalloc links the freed block onto its own pool free list, so the platform has no free to revoke. Once pymalloc returns an emptied arena to the system allocator (insert_to_freepool, when nf == ao->ntotalpools && ao->nextarena != NULL) the platform does have a free, and after a revocation sweep the stale access faults with SIGPROT si_code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG). Both outcomes are admissible; which one occurs depends on arena occupancy and sweep timing rather than on the defect, so this arm does not separate these cases. A bounds fault (si_code=1) would falsify this.

status: measured on three arms; matrix rows in results/20261006/matrix.tsv: spatial DETECTED cause=24 (spatial-20261006-105111); sublet DETECTED cause=5 (sublet-20261006-123446); cheribsd-revocation DETECTED si_code=2 (boundary-20261008-075318)
fault_sites_why: Host ASan (CPython 3.13.7 --with-address-sanitizer, PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, results/2026-10-10-asan/sites.tsv) reports heap-buffer-overflow (READ 8) at set_dealloc Objects/setobject.c:505. That run uses no Capstone arm and was recorded before any virtual arm ran.
note: ① and ③ WITHDRAWN by the 2026-10-18 review. The defect is spatial: ASan reports an 8-byte overread 8 bytes past a 216-byte region in set_dealloc (setobject.c:505). A detection is the bounds check rejecting that read -- which ② does, cause=28 CAP_OOB on `ldc a0, 0x0(s3)`, the capability load of entry->key itself. ① faults with cause=24 on `ld a1, 0x0(a0)` at address=0x7, a plain integer load THROUGH the value the read returned, and ③ with si_code=2 PROT_CHERI_TAG. Both let the defective read succeed. Measured in the guest, malloc(216) returns a capability of length 224, so offsets 216..223 are inside the bound and PROT_CHERI_BOUNDS was never possible; on ① the set is inside a pymalloc pool and mallocng bounds the pool. Host ASan shows the same split: under PYTHONMALLOC=pymalloc the overflow report disappears and only a SEGV at setobject.c:507 (Py_DECREF) remains. All three faults resolve to set_dealloc, the declared fault_site, because the read and the dereference are two lines of one function -- only the cause separates them. See ~/cpython-false-positive-examples/.
cheribsd_why_allowed: CheriBSD runs pymalloc too -- that build has WITH_PYMALLOC 1 and probe/run-cheribsd.sh sets no PYTHONMALLOC -- so on a NESTED case the object is a pymalloc block inside an arena there as well, and CheriBSD's malloc bounds the arena. That, not size-class rounding, is why the defective access succeeds on this arm; rounding is a second and much smaller effect that only matters where the object is malloc's own. Measured 2026-10-19 with tools/cheribsd/capbounds, the rounding at the sizes this corpus allocates is 16->16, 24->32, 48->48, 97->112, 100->112, 184->192, 200->224, 216->224, 400->448, 512->512, 8193->10240, 524321->655360. The 8-byte overshoot here is also three orders of magnitude too small for the representability rule that restored case 08 (a small block keeps its tag out to +16384), so si_code=2 cannot be the bounds rule arriving under the tag code. The access succeeded and the fault is downstream.
